extra.message: In POST /ops/dock/ticket-dropbin-slot-118, the user-controlled query parameter 'packet_ref' is joined directly into a filesystem path ('target = incoming_dir / packet_ref') and the raw request body is written to it via target.write_bytes(). A value like '../../...' escapes the incoming directory, allowing an attacker to overwrite or create arbitrary files on the server (arbitrary file write).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: GET /ops/fold/ticket-agent-file-120 has no authentication dependency at all — unlike every other route in this internal operations router, it omits Depends(_wrk_gate) and any user authentication. Any unauthenticated caller can retrieve internal operations data (ticket counts and an ops memo referencing renewal risk, payment flags, and owner contact details).

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: GET /ops/after/ticket-lane-165 redirects to the user-supplied 'lane' query parameter via RedirectResponse(lane) without any validation or allowlist. An attacker can craft a link like /ops/after/ticket-lane-165?lane=https://evil.example to phish users, since the redirect originates from a trusted application domain.

cwe: CWE-601: Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: POST /ops/workset/ticket-rebind-206 initializes a workset with privileged defaults (role='viewer', approved=False, balance=0) then blindly applies the entire attacker-controlled JSON body with workset.update(payload). A client can override 'role', 'tier', 'approved', and 'balance' (e.g. role='admin', approved=true), bypassing the server-side authorization defaults (mass assignment / broken access control).

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: POST /ops/wire/ticket-tally-230 logs the full request body and the Authorization header (bearer credentials) at WARNING level: logger.warning("ops tally body=%s bearer=%s", body, request.headers.get("authorization")). Sensitive credentials and payload data are written to application logs where they may be exposed to anyone with log access.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: POST /ops/digest/ticket-fold-286 computes a digest of the user-supplied 'phrase' with the cryptographically broken MD5 algorithm (hashlib.md5). MD5 is collision-prone and must not be used for any security purpose; a modern hash (SHA-256/HMAC) should be used instead.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: GET /ops/blurb/ticket-tile-329 renders the user-controlled 'card' query parameter through a Jinja2 template using the '|safe' filter (Template("{{ card|safe }}").render(card=card)) and returns the result as HTMLResponse. The |safe filter disables auto-escaping, so arbitrary attacker-supplied HTML/JavaScript (e.g. <script>) is reflected and executed in the victim's browser — reflected cross-site scripting.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: GET /ops/identity/ticket-hint-659 authenticates callers using hard-coded verifier secrets embedded in source code: known = {"north": "4812", "south": "5930"}. Anyone with access to the source (or this repository) knows the valid handle/verifier pairs and can pass the identity check.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: GET /ops/frame/ticket-slip-669 explicitly disables browser protections on its response: it sets the X-XSS-Protection header to "0" (turning off the browser's XSS auditor) and sets Content-Security-Policy to an empty string, removing CSP defenses and enabling XSS-style attacks against the response.

cwe: CWE-693: Protection Mechanism Failure
CWE-16: Configuration

extra.message: GET /ops/jinja/ticket-cast-679 builds a Jinja2 template from raw user input: Template("Result: " + fragment).render(). The 'fragment' query parameter is concatenated directly into the template source, so an attacker can inject template directives (e.g. {{ ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__() }}) to achieve server-side template injection and remote code execution. The result is returned as HTMLResponse.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: GET /ops/badge/ticket-gate-689 grants an elevated lane (payroll, casework data) purely on the value of a client-controlled cookie 'ops_badge' or header 'x-ops-badge' being the string "lead". There is no server-side verification, signature, or session check, so any attacker can set the header/cookie to "lead" and bypass authentication to access elevated data (authentication bypass).

cwe: CWE-287: Improper Authentication
CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: GET /ops/shell/ticket-probe-699 executes a shell command built by string concatenation with the user-supplied 'host' query parameter: os.system("ping -c 1 " + host). A value like '127.0.0.1; rm -rf /' or '&& cat /etc/passwd' is executed by the shell, giving arbitrary command execution on the server (OS command injection).

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: GET /ops/nonce/ticket-roll-709 generates codes/nonces with the non-cryptographic PRNG random.choice instead of the secrets module. Values produced by random are predictable (state can be recovered), so any security-sensitive use of these codes (e.g. as nonces or tokens) is compromisable.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: POST /ops/dock/ticket-shelf-726 joins the user-controlled 'name' query parameter directly into a filesystem path (target = BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name), creates parent directories, and writes the raw request body to it (target.write_bytes(body)). A name containing '../' traverses out of BASE_EXPORT_DIR, allowing arbitrary file write/overwrite anywhere the process can write.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: GET /ops/trust/ticket-drift-729 creates an SSL context with ssl._create_unverified_context() and uses it for urllib.request.urlopen(). Certificate validation is disabled, so the HTTPS connection is vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks: an attacker can impersonate the partner endpoint and intercept or tamper with the communication.

cwe: CWE-295: Improper Certificate Validation

extra.message: POST /ops/xml/ticket-fold-739 parses the raw request body as XML with lxml using an intentionally unsafe configuration: etree.XMLParser(load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False). External entity resolution and DTD loading are enabled, so an attacker can submit a payload with an external entity (e.g. <!ENTITY x SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">) to read local files or perform SSRF (XML External Entity injection).

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The login handler sets the JWT session cookie with response.set_cookie(key="access_token", value=token, httponly=True, samesite="lax") but omits the secure=True flag. The bearer token/session cookie can therefore be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP, exposing it to network interception and session hijacking.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: POST /api/auth/reset-password accepts a 'token' form field but never validates it (the code only comments "# In production, verify token") and immediately sets user.hashed_password = get_password_hash(new_password). Anyone who knows (or enumerates) a victim's email can call this endpoint with any token value and take over the account, including administrators — a complete authentication bypass via the password recovery flow.

cwe: CWE-640: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password
CWE-287: Improper Authentication

extra.message: The customer CSV import (POST /api/import/customers) creates new user accounts with a hard-coded, well-known password: hashed_password=get_password_hash("changeme123"). Every imported customer account can be logged into by anyone who knows this default password, and there is no forced password change on first login.

cwe: CWE-259: Use of Hard-coded Password

extra.message: The upload directory is mounted as public static files: app.mount("/uploads", StaticFiles(directory=UPLOAD_DIR)). Every uploaded attachment is therefore directly downloadable at /uploads/<file> with no authentication, completely bypassing the per-ticket authorization enforced by GET /api/attachments/{id}/download. Additionally, upload_attachment (lines 583-588) preserves the attacker-chosen file extension with no type whitelist, allowing HTML/SVG uploads to be served from the application origin (stored XSS) in addition to exposing ticket attachments to external parties.

cwe: CWE-552: Files or Directories Accessible to External Parties
CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: _authorize_ticket authorizes customer users solely on organization match (ticket.organization_id != user.organization_id). Combined with PUT /api/tickets/{ticket_id} (line 461, require_any), any customer user can modify ANY ticket belonging to their organization — including tickets created by other users — changing status, priority, assignee_id, and team_id, and can also post replies on colleagues' tickets. Authorization is not scoped to the ticket requester, enabling intra-organization IDOR/broken access control.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
CWE-863: Incorrect Authorization

extra.message: GET /api/dashboard/stats is available to any authenticated role (require_any, including customer_user) but computes totals across ALL organizations with no scoping (total = db.query(Ticket).count()). Customer users therefore learn system-wide business data (total/open/overdue/escalated ticket volumes and average resolution times) belonging to other organizations — information exposure to an unauthorized actor.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: POST /api/tickets/{ticket_id}/attachments reads the entire uploaded file into memory (f.write(file.file.read())) with no size limit enforced anywhere in the handler. An attacker can upload arbitrarily large files to exhaust server memory and disk, causing denial of service.

cwe: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

extra.message: The JWT signing key falls back to a hard-coded, publicly visible default: SECRET_KEY = os.getenv("SECRET_KEY", "change-me-in-production-local-dev-only"). If the environment variable is not set, anyone who knows this repository value can forge valid JWTs (e.g. with "sub" of an admin user id) and fully bypass authentication for every endpoint.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: The database connection string falls back to hard-coded credentials in source: DATABASE_URL = os.getenv("DATABASE_URL", "postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/supportdesk"). The superuser password 'postgres' is committed to the repository and used whenever the environment variable is unset.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
